race_context: South Dearborn Community School Corporation (SDCSC) is based in Aurora in Dearborn County; after the 2025 closure of Manchester Elementary it runs four schools, including Aurora and Dillsboro elementaries, South Dearborn Middle School and South Dearborn High School {ec_ross_letter}{ec_manchester_why}{ec_pog}. State enrollment counts fell from 2,345 students in 2018-19 to 1,849 in 2024-25 and 1,822 in 2025-26 {idoe_enroll}.

Superintendent: Dr. Janet Platt has been interim superintendent since Sept. 8, 2026, when the board approved a 'mutually agreeable separation agreement' with Superintendent Dr. Ronald Ross; the district said it would search for a permanent superintendent {ec_interim}. Platt attended her first board meeting as interim superintendent Sept. 15 {reg_platt}.

The board has seven members; those listed at the Aug. 18, 2026 meeting were Jeff Lane, Steve Hamlett, Shawn Spindler, Scott Willoughby (president), Kelli Gentrup-Pettit, Daryl Cutter and Brandon Messmore {ec_aug18}. Seats are elected on a staggered cycle: four members were elected in 2020 and 2024 and three in 2022 {enr_2020}{enr_2022}{enr_2024}. In 2012, Eagle Country described District 1 as Caesar Creek, Clay, Hogan and Washington townships, District 2 as Manchester and Sparta townships (two members elected that year) and District 3 as Center Township {ec_2012}; this guide did not confirm the current map.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: District 1, District 3 and At Large, one seat each, matching the state list's 'vote for 1' {in_list}{dc_candlist}. These are the three seats filled in 2022 by Jeffery Allen Lane, Scott A. Willoughby and Amber L. Probst {enr_2022}. Lane (District 1) and Willoughby (District 3) are running again. Probst resigned in July 2025, and the board appointed Brandon Messmore to finish her term; he is running in the At Large race {ec_probst}{ec_messmore}{ic_list}. Every race is contested.

Party labels: 2026 is the first year Indiana school board candidates could list a party. Five of the six South Dearborn candidates filed as Republicans; Jeff Lane declared no party {ic_list}{in_list}.

Building closures (2025): the board voted 6-1 on April 15, 2025 to close Manchester Elementary, which had 140 students in a building designed for 400; the district projected savings of about $1 million and promised all staff positions elsewhere {ec_manchester_vote}. Ross cited declining enrollment, 'the loss of revenue stemming from Senate Bill 1' and costly capital needs at the building {ec_ross_letter}. Moores Hill Elementary closed in 2021 {ec_manchester_vote}. In September 2026 the board approved selling the Manchester building {ec_interim}. Ross said in October 2025 that there were no plans to close Dillsboro Elementary {ec_dillsboro_rumor}.

Strategic plan (2025-26): the board approved strategic-plan goals including staff recruitment and retention and 'a clear, consistent district vision, curriculum and graduate profile,' and the district held public input sessions on a 'Profile of a Graduate' in January 2026 {ec_pog}.

Leadership and transparency (Aug.-Sept. 2026): about 200 people attended the Aug. 18, 2026 board meeting, most to speak about a personnel action at Dillsboro Elementary, and some speakers blamed falling enrollment on the superintendent and board members {ec_aug18}. An online petition calling for 'accountability, transparency, and leadership change' had nearly 300 signatures by Aug. 20 {ec_petition}. The board said it could not discuss personnel matters publicly; the matter was resolved Aug. 24, and on Sept. 8 the board approved the separation agreement with Ross {ec_board_stmt}{ec_lifted}{ec_interim}.

Budget: apart from Ross's April 2025 reference to lost revenue from Senate Bill 1, this guide found no reporting on SDCSC's 2026 budget, any referendum plans or test-score and accountability results {ec_ross_letter}.

Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or campaign website for any South Dearborn candidate. The district website could not be loaded, and the Dearborn County Register's coverage is behind a paywall.

background: Elected to the board in November 2022 as 'Scott A Willoughby' with 3,073 votes {enr_2022}. He was board president at the Aug. 18, 2026 meeting {ec_aug18}.
on_incumbent: Is a current board member and the board's president. At the Aug. 18, 2026 meeting, where about 200 people came to speak about a Dillsboro Elementary personnel matter, he said the meeting would be extended if needed so everyone who wanted to speak could do so {ec_aug18}. The board said in an Aug. 21 statement that it was 'continuing to gather information' and would 'make decisions based on the facts', and in September 2026 it approved a separation agreement with Superintendent Ron Ross and named an interim superintendent {ec_board_stmt}{ec_interim}. This guide found no statement attributed to Willoughby personally on those decisions.

candidates.summary: Appointed board member since August 2025, running for a full term as a Republican {ec_messmore}{in_list}.
background: Auto finance manager for the Mark Williams Group, with a career in automotive sales and management; graduate of East Central High School with a business communications degree from Northern Kentucky University, according to the district's announcement of his appointment {ec_messmore}.
Lives in Aurora, where he moved in 2011; parent of students in the district, including a recent South Dearborn graduate {ec_messmore}.

In April 2019, Eagle Country reported that parent Brandon Messmore spoke at a board work session on falling enrollment and facility needs, saying everybody had a reason to want South Dearborn's schools to succeed {ec_2019}.
path_to_ballot: The board appointed him in August 2025 to serve the rest of the term of Amber Probst, who resigned in July 2025 for personal reasons {ec_probst}{ec_messmore}.
Filed May 19, 2026 as a Republican, the first of the six South Dearborn candidates to file {dc_candlist}{ic_list}{in_list}.
on_incumbent: Is a current board member (appointed). On his appointment he said, 'South Dearborn offers so much to our kids, and I am committed to maintaining and growing those opportunities' {ec_messmore}. He sat on the board during the August 2026 Dillsboro Elementary personnel matter and the September 2026 superintendent change; this guide found no statement from him personally on either {ec_aug18}{ec_interim}.
plans: At his appointment he said his goal was 'to help ensure every student has an enjoyable, fulfilling school experience that builds a strong foundation for lifelong success' {ec_messmore}.
gaps: No campaign website, questionnaire or forum appearance found.
Whether the At Large race is the same seat Messmore holds by appointment is inferred from the 2022 results and the appointment notice, not confirmed by the district.

review_flags.person: Kyle Miller (Dillsboro Elementary principal; not a candidate)
review_flags.summary: Eagle Country reported that Miller was placed on administrative leave in August 2026; speakers at the Aug. 18, 2026 board meeting suggested it was for insubordination, which the outlet said was not verified, and the superintendent and board said personnel matters were confidential {ec_aug18}{ec_petition}. The board said Aug. 21 that it had made 'multiple attempts to communicate' with Miller and assigned Mary Bailey as principal on duty {ec_board_stmt}. On Aug. 24 the board announced she would return to work that day {ec_lifted}. No public statement from Miller was found.
review_flags.note: This was the main board controversy before the election and involved the decisions of three incumbents on the ballot (Lane, Willoughby, Messmore), but none was quoted individually. The race_context mentions it only as 'a personnel action at Dillsboro Elementary,' without the name or the allegation.

review_flags.person: Dr. Ronald Ross (former SDCSC superintendent; not a candidate)
review_flags.summary: On Sept. 8, 2026 the board approved a 'mutually agreeable separation agreement' with Ross with no discussion at the meeting, thanked him for his service and named Dr. Janet Platt interim superintendent {ec_interim}. Eagle Country said the change came after the principal's suspension {ec_interim}. The Dearborn County Register reported Oct. 8 that the interim superintendent received a stipend (full article paywalled) {reg_platt}.
review_flags.note: The terms of the separation and the reasons for it are not public in sources read. The race_context states the separation neutrally, using the district's own wording.
